description.value: The study investigated sex-specific neural responses to sexually explicit material (SEM) and cues of SEM, and examined whether trait sexual motivation, extent of SEM use, and age at onset of goal-oriented SEM use predicted neural responses.

spans.text: Therefore, the present study aimed at investigating the sex specific neural correlates towards SEM and SEM cues.

value: We expect that sexual cues as well as SEM would trigger neural activation in the reward circuit.

Further, according our main hypothesis, we expect men to have stronger activations in the reward circuit towards cues of SEM than women, which assumedly underlie the more frequent use of SEM in men as compared to women.

Based on former results from different research approaches showing greater attention deployment by SEM in subjects with high trait sexual motivation ( ), we expect a positive correlation between neural responses, especially in the reward system during SEM cues as well as during SEM processing and trait sexual motivation.
Based on various studies ( ) we further expect a positive correlation between the extent of SEM use and neural activity in the reward system towards SEM and also to sexual cues.

Initiated by findings that younger age at onset of goal-oriented pornography use might be an important vulnerability factor for later problematic use of SEM ( ) we hypothesized a negative correlation between age at onset of goal-oriented pornography use and time regularly spent on pornography use assumedly associated with corresponding correlates in the neural activity in the reward circuit.

description.value: A group of 70 healthy participants, including 33 women and 37 men, completed an event-related fMRI experiment involving cues and presentations of SEM and neutral stimuli.

description.value: Functional MRI data were processed in SPM12 and Matlab 2012a. The pipeline included unwarping and realignment for motion correction, slice-time correction, coregistration to each participant's anatomical image, normalization to the MNI standard brain with resampling to 2-mm isotropic voxels, and 6-mm FWHM Gaussian smoothing. Outlying volumes were identified with a distribution-free approach and modeled as regressors of no interest in the first-level GLM.

model_settings.value: First-level regressors modeled expectation cues as 0-second events and stimulus presentations as 8-second boxcar functions; all regressors were convolved with the canonical HRF. Six motion regressors, rating-period regressors, and corrupted-volume regressors were included as nuisance regressors. Time series were high-pass filtered with a 128-second time constant. ROI analyses used SPM small-volume correction with family-wise error correction; exploratory whole-brain analyses used FWE correction at p<.05.
